text:
B: Hello! Hi, can you hear me?
A: Yeah. Alright?
B: Yes, good, thank you. I'm Agnieszka, in Basingstoke.
A: Lee. Bridgwater.
B: Somerset, yes? Is it near Taunton? I think I spoke to... no, sorry, that was someone else.
A: Up the road from Taunton, yeah. You'll have had Joanne, maybe. Nice woman.
B: No, not yet, but she looked very nice in the photo. What do you do?
A: Mechanic. Independent garage. You in an office?
B: Yes, executive assistant, for a finance director at insurance company. Very boring for you, probably.
A: Didn't say that. Thought you looked like accounts or summat.
B: Close! I do some budget things. My husband, Tomasz, he's maintenance engineer, distribution centre. He fixes everything at home also. Our car, it's making a noise at the moment, like a sort of, erm, clunk, when we go over speed bumps.
A: Front or back?
B: Front, I think. Front side, the left.
A: Sounds like a drop link or an anti-roll bar bush, nine times out of ten. Cheap part. If a garage tells you it's the whole strut, get a second opinion. People get fobbed off with that all the time, do you know what I mean? They see someone who don't know cars and they add two hundred quid.
B: Oh, that's so useful, thank you. I will tell Tomasz. He says it's nothing, but I worry.
A: Probably is nothing. Don't leave it forever, mind.
B: What do you drive yourself?
A: Golf GTI, twenty-twelve. Done a few bits to it. Remap, exhaust, wheels. Still paying it off, mind.
B: Oh, very fast, then.
A: Fast enough. Not that you can go fast anywhere, M5's a car park half the time.
B: For us it's the Ringway in the morning. Every day, same queue, same roundabout. I listen to Polish radio and I just, you know, breathe.
A: Polish, yeah? How long you been over?
B: Since 2007. I was twenty-three. My parents are still in Rzeszów, I fly twice a year.
A: Fair play. Don't think I could do that, I've never been further than Lanzarote. All my lot's within fifteen mile.
B: That's nice, having everybody close. Sometimes I'm jealous of that, honestly.
A: Yeah, can be a bit much, Sunday dinner at my mum's every week. Still. Wouldn't swap it.
B: No. Sorry, I'm asking so many questions, is that okay?
A: You're alright. Better than the last one, she was asking what I eat.
B: Oh no! I won't ask that, I promise.
A: Cheers. Drop link, remember. Tell your fella.
B: Drop link. I'm writing it down now. I think we have one minute.
